newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market rates unmoved in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market rates unmoved in thin trade.

text.p: The Dutch money market lived through a quiet trading session on Monday, with its rates unchanged from Friday.
Call money changed hands at around 3.12 percent, sticking to the high level it reached at the beginning of the new, shorter than usual, secured loans quota, dealers said.
They said trade was very calm in all maturities, adding there was little or no trade in Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) either.
One month-deposits were quoted around 3.08/16 percent on Monday afternoon, while one year-deposits were 3.34/42 percent bid/ask, both unchanged from Friday.
One dealer said he expected the Dutch money market to remain quiet.
"The rather flat yield curve gives little incentive to invest in the longer end. The mark/guilder rate is stable...the special advances rate will remain the same," he said.
The guilder was fractionally weaker against the mark, quoting 112.4070 per 100 marks, down from 112.404 on Friday.
